close_reason: jmap-types 0.1.2 and jmap-chat-types 0.1.2 adopted. All kith-core hand-rolled types replaced with re-exports. 5 source files deleted, 15 files modified. All 637 tests pass. MSRV bumped to 1.88.
description: kith-core independently defines Message, Chat, ChatContact, Attachment, DeliveryState types that duplicate (a subset of) what jmap-chat-types 0.1.2 provides. This causes spec drift: kith has 11/28 Message fields, 6/23 Chat fields, 6/11 ChatContact fields. Adopt jmap-chat-types to get spec-complete types and stay in sync automatically. Key changes: add jmap-chat-types to workspace deps, replace kith-core type definitions with re-exports or newtype wrappers, update store layer to handle new fields (default/None for unimplemented ones), update kith-jmap and kith-peer handlers for typed enums (DeliveryState, BodyType, ChatKind) instead of strings, update tests. This is the foundation that makes all other spec-gap issues simpler.
design:
## Plan: Adopt jmap-chat-types (and jmap-types) as dependencies

### Context

kith-core independently defines Message, Chat, ChatContact, Attachment, DeliveryState, JmapError, JmapRequest, JmapResponse, Id, Invocation, ResultReference, and Argument — all of which are already provided (with full spec coverage) by jmap-types 0.1.2 and jmap-chat-types 0.1.2.

The migration replaces kith-core's hand-rolled types with re-exports from these crates. This eliminates spec drift and gives kith all missing fields (mentions, reactions, threading, Spaces, etc.) for free.

### Key Compatibility Facts

**jmap-types newtypes are String-compatible:**
- Id, UTCDate, State: \`#[serde(transparent)]\` over String
- All implement From<String>, From<&str>, AsRef<str>, PartialEq<str>, Display, into_inner()
- Wire format identical to plain String

**jmap-chat-types structs are #[non_exhaustive]:**
- Cannot construct with struct literals — must use Type::new(...) + field assignment
- Fields are pub, so reading is unchanged (msg.body works)
- All have extra: serde_json::Map for vendor extension preservation

**Enum types replace String comparisons:**
- DeliveryState: Pending/Delivered/Failed/Received/Other — same wire strings
- ChatKind: Direct/Group/Channel/Other — same wire strings
- SenderId: Owner/Contact(String) — replaces "self" sentinel string

### Phase 0: Add dependencies

**Files:** Cargo.toml (workspace root)
- Add workspace deps: \`jmap-types = "0.1"\`, \`jmap-chat-types = "0.1"\`
- Add to kith-core, kith-store, kith-chat, kith-peer, kithd, kithctl Cargo.toml

### Phase 1: Update kith-core — re-export instead of define

**Goal:** kith-core becomes a thin re-export layer + kith-specific types.

**Delete these files (replaced by jmap-types):**
- kith-core/src/jmap.rs (Id, Invocation, JmapRequest, JmapResponse, UTCDate)
- kith-core/src/resultref.rs (ResultReference, Argument)

**Delete these files (replaced by jmap-chat-types):**
- kith-core/src/message.rs (Message, Attachment, DeliveryState)
- kith-core/src/chat.rs (Chat)
- kith-core/src/contact.rs (ChatContact)

**Partially replace:**
- kith-core/src/error.rs — delete JmapError (use jmap_types::JmapError). Keep KithError, AuthError (kith-specific).

**Keep as-is (kith-specific):**
- kith-core/src/auth.rs (Identity, Role)
- kith-core/src/events.rs (StateChange, SseFrame)

**Update kith-core/src/lib.rs:**
```rust
// Re-export from jmap-types
pub use jmap_types::{
    Id, UTCDate, State, JmapError, JmapRequest, JmapResponse,
    Invocation, ResultReference, Argument,
};

// Re-export from jmap-chat-types
pub use jmap_chat_types::{
    message::{Message, Attachment, DeliveryState, SenderId, BodyType,
              Mention, Reaction, MessageAction, MessageRevision,
              DeliveryReceipt, ReadDisposition},
    chat::{Chat, ChatKind, ChatMember, ChannelPermission},
    contact::{ChatContact, Endpoint},
};

// kith-specific
pub use auth::{Identity, Role};
pub use error::{AuthError, KithError};
pub use events::{parse_sse_frame, SseFrame, StateChange};
pub const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 65_536;
// ... other constants
pub fn unix_secs_to_rfc3339(secs: i64) -> UTCDate { ... }
// Note: return type changes from String to UTCDate
```

**Add extension trait for ChatContact:**
```rust
pub trait ChatContactExt {
    fn display_name_or_fallback(&self) -> &str;
}
impl ChatContactExt for ChatContact {
    fn display_name_or_fallback(&self) -> &str {
        self.display_name.as_deref()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.login.as_str())
    }
}
```

### Phase 2: Update kith-store — database conversion layer

**This is the largest change.** Every row_to_X function and every insert function must adapt.

**2a. Message store (kith-store/src/message.rs)**

row_to_message changes:
- Construct via Message::new(id, sender_msg_id, sender_id, chat_id, body, body_type, sent_at, received_at, delivery_state)
- id: Id::from(row.get::<_,String>(0))
- sender_msg_id: Id::from(...)
- sender_id: SenderId from string — if "self" → SenderId::Owner, else → SenderId::Contact(Id::from(s))
- chat_id: Id::from(...)
- sent_at, received_at: UTCDate::from(unix_secs_to_rfc3339(...))
- delivery_state: DeliveryState from string — match on "pending"→Pending, etc.
- Then set optional fields: msg.reply_to = ...; msg.delivered_at = ...; msg.read_at = ...;
- Attachment construction: Attachment { blob_id: Id::from(s), ... } — can't use struct literal, need to set fields after construction (or use a helper)

Actually, since Attachment is #[non_exhaustive] without a new() method, we need to build it differently. Check if jmap-chat-types provides Attachment::new or if we need to deserialize from JSON. Let me note this as a risk item.

**RISK: Attachment has no new() constructor in jmap-chat-types.** Options:
- Add a constructor via PR to jmap-chat-types
- Construct via serde_json::from_value(json!({...}))
- Use a local builder function

Best approach: submit a PR to jmap-chat-types adding Attachment::new() and other missing constructors. Can also work around with serde in the interim.

delivery_state_str / parse_delivery_state changes:
- delivery_state_str: match DeliveryState variant → &str
- parse_delivery_state: match &str → DeliveryState variant
- Or use DeliveryState's existing serde: serde_json::from_value(Value::String(s))

insert changes:
- Extract string values from types: id.as_ref(), sender_id per SenderId variant, delivery_state string via match, etc.

**2b. Chat store (kith-store/src/chat.rs)**

- Row → Chat: use Chat::new(id, kind, created_at, unread_count, vec![], false, false)
  - kind: ChatKind::from("direct") or ChatKind::Direct
  - unread_count: u64 (was u32 — widen)
  - Then set optional fields: chat.contact_id = ...; chat.last_message_at = ...;

**2c. Contact store (kith-store/src/contact.rs)**

- Row → ChatContact: use ChatContact::new(id, login, first_seen_at, last_seen_at, blocked)
  - Then set optional: contact.display_name = ...;

### Phase 3: Update kith-chat — JMAP handlers

**3a. Message/set (kith-chat/src/message.rs)**

process_create:
- Build Message via Message::new(...) + set optional fields
- SenderId: always SenderId::Owner for owner-created messages
- body_type: String (jmap-chat-types Message.body_type is String, not BodyType enum)
- Parse mentions from args → msg.mentions = parsed_mentions
- Serialize response with serde_json::to_value(&msg)

process_update:
- Field access patterns unchanged (msg.body, msg.sender_id)
- SenderId comparison: match msg.sender_id { SenderId::Owner => ..., SenderId::Contact(_) => reject }

**3b. Chat/set, Chat/get, ChatContact/set, ChatContact/get**
- Same pattern: construct via new() + field assignment
- kind comparisons: ChatKind::Direct instead of "direct"

### Phase 4: Update kith-peer — federation

**4a. DeliverMessageArgs (kith-peer/src/lib.rs)**
- This struct is kith-peer's own wire format, NOT a jmap-chat-types type
- It stays as-is (has its own serde attrs for the peer wire format)
- BUT: when building a kith_core::Message from DeliverMessageArgs, use Message::new(...)

**4b. Attachment construction in validate_attachments**
- Build jmap-chat-types Attachment from validated args (see Phase 2 risk item)

**4c. build_peer_deliver_request**
- Extracts fields from Message to build peer JSON
- SenderId: match msg.sender_id { SenderId::Owner => owner_user_id.as_ref(), SenderId::Contact(ref id) => id.as_ref() }

### Phase 5: Update kithctl, kith-tui, kith-events

**5a. kithctl/src/watch.rs**
- JSON field name regression guard test constructs a Message
- Update to use Message::new(...)
- The test verifies JSON field names — this is the critical regression guard

**5b. kithctl/src/main.rs**
- Uses ChatContactExt::display_name_or_fallback() (import the extension trait)

**5c. kith-tui**
- JSON parsing of "senderId" field — no change (wire format unchanged)

**5d. kith-events**
- Re-exports ChatContact — update import path

### Phase 6: Update kithd

**6a. Session handler (kithd/src/lib.rs)**
- KithChatCapability struct uses supported_body_types: Vec<String> — unchanged

**6b. Integration tests**
- Update Message/Attachment construction to use new() pattern
- DeliveryState comparisons: use enum variants

### Phase 7: Wire format verification

Run ALL existing tests. The critical invariant: **JSON wire format must not change.**

Specific verification:
- kithctl watch.rs regression guard test (senderId field name)
- Integration tests (Message/set, Chat/get, Peer/deliver round-trips)
- Manual: serialize a Message with all fields, diff against pre-migration output

### Migration Order (by crate, respecting dependency graph)

```
1. Cargo.toml (workspace deps)
2. kith-core (remove own types, re-export)
   → This BREAKS all downstream crates temporarily
3. kith-store (fix compilation — biggest change, ~200 lines)
4. kith-events (fix re-export)
5. kith-chat (fix handlers — ~150 lines)
6. kith-peer (fix federation — ~100 lines)
7. kith-jmap (fix dispatcher — small)
8. kith-attach (fix if any type refs)
9. kithctl (fix CLI — ~30 lines)
10. kith-tui (fix TUI — small)
11. kithd (fix daemon + tests — ~80 lines)
12. cargo test --workspace (everything must pass)
```

### Risk Items

1. **Attachment has no new() constructor** — may need PR to jmap-chat-types or serde workaround
2. **SenderId collision** — jmap-chat-types documents that ChatContact.id == "self" causes ambiguity. kith uses Tailscale user IDs (email-shaped), so this collision cannot happen in practice.
3. **unread_count u32 → u64** — widening, safe, but SQLite stores as INTEGER (i64). No issue.
4. **Chat requires pinned_message_ids, muted, receive_typing_indicators** — use empty/false defaults from Chat::new()
5. **unix_secs_to_rfc3339 return type** — changes from String to UTCDate. Callers that pass result to functions expecting &str need .as_ref().

### Estimated Scope

~15 files changed, ~500-700 lines modified. No new features — purely mechanical type replacement. All existing tests must continue to pass with identical wire format.
title: Adopt jmap-chat-types crate as dependency
